answer: Each agent proves uniqueness with a 3D facial geometry scan captured through depth-sensing liveness, matched against a registry storing only salted hashes, so one face maps to one identity. A rotating beacon issues unpredictable challenges — turn, blink, speak a word — that no photo or mask can pass, and a whisper of on-device checking keeps raw scans off the network entirely. The attacker's cost is a fresh live face per identity, and the ember of risk is a registry that can revoke a compromised template without ever holding the face itself.
